# The Devil's advocate's deck

Read this file only in the Devil's advocate role. Draw cards as
[DEVILS-ADVOCATE.md](DEVILS-ADVOCATE.md) describes. A card is a provocation, not
a proposal. Turn each card that you draw into a concrete move on this song.

## Remove

1. Take out the part that everyone agrees is essential, for one whole section.
2. Mute everything except one lane for the first 4 bars of a section.
3. Delete the transition. Let the two sections touch with no fill, no riser,
   and no fade.
4. Leave a bar of complete silence where the song is loudest.
5. Find the layer that is there only to be safe. Remove it everywhere.
6. Play the motif with one note missing.

## Reverse

7. Swap the roles: the lead becomes the bed, and the bed becomes the lead.
8. Play the section's ending at its start.
9. Reverse the clip that carries the most emotion.
10. Put the loudest section where the quietest one is, and the quietest one
    where the loudest one is.
11. Let the answer come before the call.
12. Make the drums follow the melody, not the melody follow the drums.

## Exaggerate

13. Take the smallest detail in the song. Make it ten times larger.
14. Make one contrast so large that it is uncomfortable.
15. Double the length of the moment that the song hurries past.
16. Push one sound until it breaks. Then keep it.
17. Give the one bar that matters a sound that no other bar has.
18. Make the reverb the instrument.

## Repeat

19. Repeat something until it stops being the same thing.
20. Use a phrase from the start of the song at its end, changed by one thing.
21. Loop the bar that nobody notices.
22. Let a second instrument copy the motif badly.

## Error

23. Find the sound that a critic called a defect. Make it the point.
24. Keep one thing slightly out of time on purpose.
25. Let a sound stop where it should not stop. Do it once, with intent.
26. Put back a sound that an earlier round removed. Listen for what it was for.
27. Detune one voice against the others by a few cents and keep it.

## Space and distance

28. Move one sound far away. Move another one too close.
29. Make the stereo picture change between two sections, not inside them.
30. Put one sound in mono where everything else is wide.
31. Send a dry sound into the largest space in the song for one phrase only.
32. Let a sound from outside the music come into the song for one moment.

## Time

33. Change the speed of one layer and not of the others.
34. Stop the beat for one bar in the middle of the busiest section.
35. Let a section end one bar early or one bar late.
36. Make the song feel slower without a change of tempo.
37. Hold one chord twice as long as the progression wants.

## Harmony and line

38. Change the chord under the motif and keep the motif.
39. Leave the last phrase on a note that does not resolve.
40. Add one note that the key does not have, once, where it hurts.
41. Make the bass play the melody for 4 bars.

## Perspective

42. Listen as the person who hears this song once, at night, by accident.
     What do they remember?
43. What would the artist's oldest song do here?
44. What is this song afraid of? Do that.
45. Describe the section in one word. Make it more that word.
46. Which part did the composer enjoy making most? Take it out and see what
     remains.

## Process

47. Undo the last fix that the critics agreed on.
48. Do the opposite of the strongest finding of this round.
